description: SurrealDB must be the primary data store for all activity data (templates, metrics, executions). Redis is a read-through cache only. Write path: Client → rpc-api → SurrealDB → Redis cache. Read path: Client → rpc-api → Redis (cache hit) OR SurrealDB (cache miss) → populate Redis.

dataFlow.write: Client → FastAPI Router → Action Layer → SurrealDB (PRIMARY) → Redis Cache (TTL)
dataFlow.read: Client → FastAPI Router → Action Layer → Redis (cache hit) OR SurrealDB (cache miss) → populate Redis → return data
dataFlow.cacheInvalidation: On write: update SurrealDB first, then update/invalidate Redis cache

compliance.status: PARTIALLY COMPLIANT - majority of code follows specification, but 3 components need refactoring

components.currentBehavior: FastAPI router that delegates to action layer for template operations. Uses Redis dependency injection.
components.desiredBehavior: Same - router is correct, delegates to action layer which handles storage.
components.role: Entry point - HTTP endpoints for template operations

components.currentBehavior: Writes to SurrealDB FIRST (line 345), then Redis cache (line 353). Includes error handling where Redis cache failure is non-fatal (line 362).
components.desiredBehavior: Write to SurrealDB first, then cache in Redis with TTL
components.role: Write path - template creation with SurrealDB primary + Redis cache

components.currentBehavior: Cache-aside pattern implemented. Checks Redis first (line 211), on miss loads from SurrealDB (line 217), populates Redis cache (lines 222-227), returns data.
components.desiredBehavior: Read from Redis first, on miss read from SurrealDB and populate cache
components.role: Read path - single template retrieval with cache-aside pattern

components.currentBehavior: Cache-aside pattern for template list. Checks Redis set (line 105), on miss queries SurrealDB (line 111), populates cache for each template (lines 120-126).
components.desiredBehavior: Read from Redis first, on miss read from SurrealDB and populate cache
components.role: Read path - template list retrieval with cache-aside pattern

components.currentBehavior: Uses DUAL-WRITE with compensating transaction. Atomically updates Redis metrics (lines 527-582), then writes to SurrealDB (lines 628-653). On SurrealDB failure, rolls back Redis (lines 665-673).
components.desiredBehavior: Write to SurrealDB FIRST, then update Redis cache. If SurrealDB fails, abort (don't cache). If Redis fails, continue (cache failure is non-fatal).
components.gap: ORDER VIOLATION - writes Redis first, then SurrealDB. Should be: SurrealDB → Redis. Current approach uses compensating transaction which adds complexity.
components.role: Write path - execution result recording with atomic updates

components.currentBehavior: Writes template to SurrealDB with deterministic record ID. No Redis caching (handled by action layer).
components.desiredBehavior: Write to SurrealDB as primary storage

components.currentBehavior: Reads from SurrealDB. No Redis handling (cache-aside pattern handled by action layer).
components.desiredBehavior: Read from SurrealDB when cache misses

components.currentBehavior: Queries all templates from SurrealDB. No Redis handling.
components.desiredBehavior: Read from SurrealDB when cache misses

components.currentBehavior: Updates metrics in SurrealDB using incremental aggregation. No Redis handling (action layer manages cache).
components.desiredBehavior: Update metrics in SurrealDB as primary storage

components.currentBehavior: Reads metrics from SurrealDB. No Redis handling.
components.desiredBehavior: Read metrics from SurrealDB when cache misses

components.currentBehavior: Writes to SurrealDB (line 98), then dual-writes to Redis (lines 101-119). Redis failure is non-fatal but creates duplicate storage.
components.desiredBehavior: Write ONLY to SurrealDB. Redis should cache reads, not receive dual-writes.
components.gap: DUAL-WRITE ANTI-PATTERN - execution records written to both SurrealDB and Redis. Should only write to SurrealDB.

components.currentBehavior: Entire service operates on Redis only. Stores execution records as Redis hashes, aggregates from Redis, stores metrics in Redis. NO SurrealDB integration.
components.desiredBehavior: Should operate on SurrealDB as primary storage with Redis as cache layer
components.gap: CRITICAL VIOLATION - bypasses SurrealDB entirely. This is Phase 2 holdover code that needs migration.

components.currentBehavior: Provides connection management and query interface for SurrealDB. No Redis coupling.
components.desiredBehavior: SurrealDB client for primary storage access
components.role: Infrastructure - SurrealDB connection and query execution

violations.issue: Entire service bypasses SurrealDB and operates on Redis only
violations.impact: Metrics data stored only in Redis (no TTL, effectively becomes primary storage). Data loss if Redis fails or cache eviction occurs.
violations.recommendation: PHASE 2 MIGRATION REQUIRED: Either deprecate this service (use template_metrics.py operations instead) OR refactor to use SurrealDB as primary with Redis caching.

violations.issue: Writes Redis BEFORE SurrealDB (should be reversed)
violations.impact: If SurrealDB write fails after Redis update, requires compensating transaction rollback which can fail, causing data inconsistency.
violations.recommendation: Reverse order: Write to SurrealDB first, then update Redis cache. Remove compensating transaction complexity.

violations.issue: Dual-write to both SurrealDB and Redis for execution records
violations.impact: Redis stores execution records directly instead of caching reads from SurrealDB. Violates cache-only specification.
violations.recommendation: Remove Redis dual-write (lines 101-122). Let action layer handle caching on READ operations.

metricsCache.populatedOn: cache miss during read and on write (record_execution_result)

recommendations.details: This service is Phase 2 code that bypasses SurrealDB. Either remove it (use template_metrics.py operations) or refactor to use SurrealDB primary + Redis cache.
Change dual-write order: SurrealDB first (primary), then Redis (cache). Remove compensating transaction complexity.
Remove Redis write at lines 101-122. Execution records should only be written to SurrealDB. Redis caching should happen on READ via action layer.
Currently cache invalidation is implicit (TTL-based). Consider adding explicit invalidation on write operations for stronger consistency.
